title: a commander made in grief
hookLine: three men are all that's left of an army, and a dying king makes one of them its commander
carry: krodha, anger, is an enemy within

cards: Evening on the battlefield. Three warriors come looking for their king: Ashvatthama, the son of Drona; Kripa, the old teacher of the princes; and Kritavarma, a fighter from Krishna's own clan who fought on the other side.
They're the last of the Kaurava army still standing. They find Duryodhana where Bhima left him, his thighs broken, covered in dust, unable to rise.
The man who once commanded a vast host now has three men and a darkening sky. This is Sauptika, the book of the night.

teach.b: In Ganguli's telling, the three weep at the sight of him. Duryodhana, in pain, still speaks like a king: don't grieve; I fought and didn't turn my back. But Ashvatthama can't let it rest.
He remembers how his own father died: told a lie about his son's death, laying down his weapons, and then killed. Now he sees his king broken by a blow below the waist.
And he makes a vow, in effect: before this night is over, I'll send the Panchalas to the land of the dead.
Then Duryodhana, who can't stand and has no army, asks Kripa for a pot of water, and with it has Kripa install Ashvatthama as commander. Commander of three men.

Ashvatthama embraces the king, and the three go off into the night. Hindu teachers have a name for what was just crowned. They speak of six inner enemies, the shadripu: desire, anger, greed, delusion, pride and envy.
The second is krodha, anger. It isn't an enemy out there. It lives inside, and it can borrow grief's face, so it feels like loyalty, like love for a father or a king.
But tonight it's anger that takes command, with a vow and a pot of water.
It's the same for us when someone hurts a person we love: the hottest promises come in the first hour. The teaching doesn't say don't grieve. It says notice who's giving the orders.

how: Sauptika, from a Sanskrit word for sleep, is the name of the tenth of the Mahabharata's eighteen books, and reciters of the whole epic carry the story straight on from the fallen king into the night raid.

o: the book of the women who mourn the war's dead
the vow Ashvatthama makes before his fallen king
the book of the night, named from a word for sleep

games.q: the three survivors, and the enemy within — tap the pairs.

s: Duryodhana was already dead when the three survivors found him
he was alive and still spoke like a king.
Hindu teachers count anger among six inner enemies
krodha is one of the shadripu, with desire, greed, delusion, pride and envy.
Ashvatthama's vow came from a calm, clear mind
it came out of grief for his father and his king, and anger took command.

games.q: you're Kripa, holding the pot of water. Ashvatthama has just vowed revenge in his grief. what would the teaching of the inner enemies tell him?
o: anger dressed as loyalty is still anger. wait before you act on it.
a vow made in grief is always sacred. keep it.
anger is only a problem if you lose.
games.why: the shadripu teaching names krodha an enemy within. in the story, though, the water is poured, and anger takes command.

practice: Sit and feel where heat collects when you're angry: the chest, the jaw, the hands. Many Hindus close their prayers with om shanti shanti shanti, peace said three times. Breathing in, notice the heat without feeding it.
Breathing out, say shanti silently: once for your body, once for your words, once for whoever you're angry with. If you don't pray, let the word simply mean peace.

wordCard.voice: Sauptika. The book of the night: three survivors, a broken king, a vow made in grief, and anger crowned with a pot of water.

orig.note: commander of the army: the title Duryodhana gives Ashvatthama with a pot of water.

carryVoice: Your line: krodha, anger, is an enemy within. Tomorrow, under a banyan tree, one man can't sleep. That's day eight hundred forty-nine.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Shalya Parva (end) and Sauptika Parva (opening), the three survivors find Duryodhana, Ashvatthama's vow and his installation as commander
